questions.stem: What does the L in PESTLE stand for?
options: Legal
Labour
Location
Logistics
questions.why: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental. Legal covers employment, consumer, environmental, competition and intellectual property law.
whyNot: Labour issues fall under social or legal depending on the aspect.
Location is not a PESTLE category.
Logistics is an operational matter.

questions.stem: Which of Porter's five forces refers to customers being able to force prices down?
options: Buyer power
Supplier power
Competitive rivalry
Threat of substitutes
questions.why: Buyer power is strong when there are few large buyers, the product is undifferentiated and switching is easy.
whyNot: Supplier power is about those who sell TO the business.
Rivalry is competition between existing firms.
Substitutes are different ways of meeting the same need.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of the threat of substitutes?
options: The extent to which customers could meet the same need in a different way
The number of rival brands of the same product
The likelihood of new firms entering the industry
The power of suppliers to raise prices
questions.why: A substitute meets the same need differently: a video call instead of a flight, a bicycle instead of a car. It is not a rival brand of the same product.
whyNot: Rival brands are competitive rivalry, not substitutes. This is the most common confusion on this topic.
That is the threat of new entrants.
That is supplier power.

questions.stem: Porter's five forces framework is used to analyse:
options: how profitable an industry is and why
how strong one particular firm is
which products a business should sell
the internal strengths of a business
questions.why: It explains industry profitability. Where all five forces are strong, profit is competed away for everyone in it. A strong firm can still do well in a bad industry.
whyNot: It analyses the industry, not the individual firm. This distinction matters.
That is portfolio analysis.
That is the internal half of a SWOT.

questions.stem: What makes the threat of new entrants strong?
options: Low barriers to entry, such as small capital requirements and no licensing
High capital requirements and strong brand loyalty
Economies of scale enjoyed by existing firms
Exclusive access to distribution held by incumbents
questions.why: Where entry is cheap and easy, competitors arrive quickly. That is why online markets are so crowded.
whyNot: Those are barriers, which make the threat weak.
A barrier: newcomers cannot match incumbent costs.
Also a barrier.

options: Few suppliers, no substitutes for their input, and costly switching
Many competing suppliers offering identical inputs
Suppliers desperate to win business
Buyers able to produce the input themselves
questions.why: Where a supplier is one of few and their input is critical, they can raise prices or reduce quality without losing the business.
whyNot: Many interchangeable suppliers means weak supplier power.
Desperate suppliers have little power.
Backward integration reduces supplier power.

questions.stem: Why are guesthouse margins thinner than headline room rates suggest, in five forces terms?
options: Four or five of the forces are strong, so profit is competed away
Rivalry is the only strong force
Supplier power is the only strong force
All five forces are weak
questions.why: High rivalry between similar properties, high buyer power through easy online comparison and platform commission, moderate to high supplier power on imports and transfers, low barriers to entry, and many substitutes. Strong forces mean thin profits for everyone.
whyNot: Buyer power, entry and substitutes are all strong too.
Rivalry and buyer power are at least as strong.
If they were weak, margins would be high and sustainable.

questions.stem: How should PESTLE be used in an exam answer?
options: Identify the two or three factors that matter for this business and develop them into chains
List all six factors with one example each
Define each of the six letters
Use it only for large multinational businesses
questions.why: A full listing earns little. One developed technological threat is worth more than six labelled headings, because development is where the analysis marks are.
whyNot: Listing is the weakest use of the framework.
Definitions earn knowledge marks only.
It applies to businesses of any size.

questions.stem: What is the main limitation of both PESTLE and five forces?
options: They describe the current situation but do not predict what happens next or weigh the factors
They cannot be applied to service businesses
They require detailed financial data
They can only be used once a year
questions.why: Both organise what is happening and neither ranks the factors or forecasts change. Deciding which force or influence matters most is a judgement you have to make, and saying so is an evaluation point.
whyNot: Both are widely applied to services.
Both are largely qualitative.
They can be revisited whenever conditions change.
